sources.title: Jomon Culture, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum synthesis of periodization, subsistence, settlement, technologies, regional variation, and the transition toward Yayoi.

sources.title: Jomon culture, Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan
sources.note: Official World Heritage site synthesis of food, houses, graves, childhood, crafts, exchange, health, and regional pottery.

sources.title: Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan, Japan National Tourism Organization
sources.note: Official Japanese description of seventeen sites, settlement types, graves, ritual places, and regional scope.

sources.title: Oyu Stone Circles
sources.note: Official site record for two stone circles, associated structures and graves, ritual objects, and solstice interpretation.

sources.title: Isedotai Stone Circles
sources.note: Official site record for four stone circles, pillar buildings, graves, storage pits, ditches, and ritual objects.

sources.title: Kiusu Earthwork Burial Circles
sources.note: Official site record for Final Jomon communal earthwork graves, standing stones, red pigment, and labor estimates.

sources.title: Omori Katsuyama Stone Circle
sources.note: Official site record for a Final Jomon stone circle, settlement traces, ritual stones, and winter-solstice alignment.

sources.title: Kamegaoka Burial Site
sources.note: Official site record for Final Jomon graves, wetland deposits, lacquer, jade, pottery, and goggle-eyed figurines.

sources.title: Korekawa Site
sources.note: Official site record for a Final Jomon settlement, graves, mounds, wetland preservation, foods, and lacquered wooden objects.

sources.title: Goggle-eyed dogu, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum record for a hollow Final Jomon figurine from Tohoku and the uncertainty surrounding dogu functions.

sources.title: Bow nock, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum record for a Final Jomon bone bow fitting associated with hunting equipment.

sources.title: Horned-owl dogu, e-Museum
sources.note: National museum record for a Late or Final Jomon Kanto figurine with red color and modeled hair, clothing, and accessories.

sources.title: Infant feeding practices in prehistoric Japan
sources.note: Stable-isotope study of Yoshigo individuals modeling breastfeeding and weaning ages without asserting a special weaning diet.

sources.title: Nutritional deficiency and ecological stress in the Middle to Final western Jomon
sources.note: Peer reviewed study of possible scurvy, caries, and ecological stress among Tsukumo remains.

sources.title: Migration and ritual tooth ablation in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Strontium-isotope and tooth-ablation study from Yoshigo and Inariyama testing mobility and social interpretations.

sources.title: Ritual tooth ablation and social identity in Late Jomon Japan
sources.note: Bioarchaeological analysis treating tooth removal as bodily practice and social identity evidence with individual variation.

sources.title: Paleoparasitology and archaeology in Japan
sources.note: Review of parasite evidence, Jomon coprolites in shell middens, and uncertainty about exact toilet arrangements.

sources.title: Storage pit variability in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Study of spatial and temporal differences in storage-pit capacity rather than one uniform storage system.

sources.title: The Jomon food diversity database
sources.note: Systematic evidence for strong regional and temporal differences in plant and animal use.

sources.title: Jomon aquatic resource use and shell middens
sources.note: Study of long-term change in aquatic food acquisition and the archaeological value of shell middens.

sources.title: Seasonality and deer procurement in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Dental-radiography study testing deer hunting seasons and coast-inland movement during the Late Jomon.

sources.title: Regional dietary variation and Jomon mandibular morphology
sources.note: Bioarchaeological evidence for regional and temporal dietary variation, including limited movement of some foods.

sources.title: Plant husbandry in prehistoric eastern Japan
sources.note: Archaeobotanical assessment of plant management and cultivation without equating every Jomon community with full farming.

sources.title: Agriculture and the Yayoi transition in Japan
sources.note: Review of varied regional transitions, early rice cultivation, and interaction between hunter-gatherers and farmers.

sources.title: The spread of rice to Japan
sources.note: Bayesian chronological model showing discontinuous and regionally delayed rice-farming expansion.

sources.title: Japan considered from the hypothesis of farmer-language spread
sources.note: Genetic, linguistic, and archaeological synthesis stressing a time-transgressive transition and continuing northern Epi-Jomon trajectories.

sources.title: The introduction of rice and millet agriculture in prehistoric Japan
sources.note: Archaeobotanical study of delayed crop adoption in eastern and northern Japan and interaction between Jomon and Yayoi traditions.

sources.title: Early writing in Japan and Old Japanese sources
sources.note: Scholarly history placing established writing in Japan many centuries after the Final Jomon.

sources.title: Current studies on the Jomon period
sources.note: Archaeological review of regional variation, fishing, plant use, mortuary practices, adhesives, and long-distance exchange.

sources.title: Chemical analysis of Jomon lacquerware
sources.note: Materials analysis identifying layered Toxicodendron lacquer, drying oil, and mineral pigments.

sources.title: Reconstructing prehistoric Japanese nets from pottery impressions
sources.note: Study reconstructing plant-fiber nets from impressions in pottery near the Jomon-Yayoi transition.

sources.title: Hunting dogs as environmental adaptations in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Zooarchaeological interpretation of later Jomon dog burials and dogs as hunting partners.

sources.title: Regional population histories in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Paleodemographic synthesis showing sharply different population trajectories among Kanto, Aomori, and Hokkaido.

sources.title: Radiocarbon chronology at Okyozuka
sources.note: Regional radiocarbon study illustrating that pottery-phase chronology must be built locally rather than assumed nationwide.
